# Creating int (Integer) variable

#### Course: Learn C Programming

## Creating int (Integer) variable

Here's how we can create (declare) a variable to store our age:

```c
int age;
```

![Parts in Variable Declaration](data:image/png;base64,)

Variable declaration has two parts:

1. Data type: int
2. Name of the variable: age

The line of code above instructs the computer to reserve memory for storing a value type of int and name that memory age.

Variable declaration alone is not enough; we must also assign a value to the variable.

We'll learn how to do that next after a quiz.

##### When to use int main/int void/

![User profile picture](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

Sarthak Baral from Programiz

Good question! Understanding when to use `int main()` versus `void main()` is quite important.

In C, the standard practice is to use `int main()`. This is because the `int` return type indicates to the operating system how the program completed. When your program runs successfully, it typically returns 0, signaling that everything went as expected. This is done with the statement `return 0;` at the end of the main function. Using `void main()` is often discouraged because it doesn't return any value, which can lead to undefined behavior in some systems.

So, stick with `int main()` for a more reliable and standard-compliant C program. Hope this helps! Let me know if you have more questions.
